narrative: Material PL1__MAB0D63B exhibits stable, high-volume demand (CV=0.189, mean ~52,925 units/day) with no statistically significant trend. Lead times are moderately variable (CV=0.458, mean 2.52 days), and lead-time variance accounts for 93.6% of the safety-stock buffer requirement. The current SAP policy carries zero safety stock and replenishes at MOQ (~53K units, ~249 orders/year), creating excessive transaction costs. The recommended (r,Q) policy batches into ~20 large replenishments/year with a 103,842-unit safety buffer, reducing total annual cost by 81.1% while achieving the 95% service level target.
warnings: 3 near-zero lead-time observations (<=0.1 days) removed as data anomalies
Lead-time variance dominates sigma_LTD (93.6%): supplier/transport reliability is the key service risk
Robust safety stock (19,160) is significantly lower than parametric SS (103,842) — lead-time variability, not demand variability, is the binding constraint

research_insights.selection_rationale: Stable high-volume demand with continuous non-zero daily consumption makes a continuous-review (r,Q) policy optimal. The EOQ formula minimises total ordering and holding costs; the reorder point covers expected lead-time demand plus a z-score safety buffer calibrated to 95% service level.
research_insights.boundary_risk: The optimised policy satisfies the storage constraint: SS + OQ = 750,552 units which is well within the 1,363,206-unit capacity limit. No capacity-driven order reduction was necessary.
